verdict.rationale: Clerk documents MCP-oriented OAuth pieces as its own capability: support for both Client ID Metadata Documents and Dynamic Client Registration (clerk-docs-57), custom OAuth scopes that give MCP clients precise, discoverable access (clerk-docs-55), and OAuth scoped access for third-party apps (clerk-docs-44). However, the evidence never explicitly shows Clerk placing a spec-compliant authorization flow in front of the user's own MCP server, and the connect-mcp-client page may refer to Clerk's own hosted MCP server, so the reviewer's concern holds and the verdict stays partial. Missing for 10: explicit docs on protecting a developer's own MCP server end to end (protected-resource metadata, token verification/audience binding on the resource server), confirmation of MCP authorization-spec compliance, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
